title: Keirdyn tradishoonagh
description: Ten short stories about traditional crafts: a young apprentice in a blacksmith's workshop in Ballaugh, soap and candles made in Peel, a fisherman's jumper knitted by a grandmother in Laxey, wooden bowls of pear and cherry for a collector, a scene painter copying a bay onto canvas for a film set, a new wooden rowing boat for a Ramsey club, a beekeeper whose neighbour is stung, a fiddle made for a string quartet, the history of an old printing house in Castletown, and a man who grinds lenses for telescopes and microscopes.

lessons.title: Yn crou as y cliwe
lessons.summary: Gwenno Trembath, nineteen, asks the stern blacksmith Alun Rattray in Ballaugh for a job in his old workshop; he gives her small tasks first and then teaches her to make a horseshoe, with drops of sweat on her face by the fire; she asks about the old sword on the wall, and he tells the story of a young man who wanted revenge on the robber who killed his father, but whose bravery was to bring the robber to the court instead; she asks about the hardest metal, and he says tungsten is too hard for a smith's fire; after a month she makes a horseshoe alone.
lessons.text:
Ta Alun Rattray ny ghaaue. Ta keirdlann echey ayns Ballaugh, faggys da'n cheeill. Ta'n cheirdlann shenn as dorraghey, as ta aile mooar ayn.

'Sy tourey shoh, haink Gwenno Trembath dys y cheirdlann. T'ee nuy bleeaney jeig d'eash, as v'ee shirrey kiartag.

“Ta mee laccal gynsaghey yn cheird,” dooyrt ee.

Va Alun loghtal. “She obbyr çheh as obbyr trome t'ayn,” dooyrt eh, as e eddin loghtal. “Vel oo son gobbraghey dagh laa veih shiaght er y chlag derrey shey?”

“Ta,” dooyrt Gwenno. Myr shen, hug eh yn chiartag j'ee.

Er y chied hiaghtin, cha dooar Gwenno agh kiartagyn beggey: y laare y scughey, ny greieyn y ghlenney, as yn aile y reayll. Er y nah hiaghtin, ren Alun gynsaghey j'ee crou y yannoo.

“Ta crou cabbil jeant jeh yiarn,” dooyrt eh. “Ta shin cur yn yiarn 'syn aile derrey t'eh jiarg. Eisht ta shin bwoalley eh dy chur cummey er.” Va'n aile feer çheh. Va bineyn ollish er eddin Gwenno, as huitt bine er y yiarn jiarg. Cha row y chied chrou eck mie.

Va cliwe shenn croghey er y voalley 'sy cheirdlann. Un fastyr, dooyrt Gwenno: “Quoi ren yn cliwe shen?”

“Ren shenn-ayr my henn-ayr eh,” dooyrt Alun. “Ta skeeal ayn mychione y chliwe. Va fer aeg ayns Ballaugh, as va'n ayr echey er ny varroo liorish roosteyr. Va'n fer aeg laccal cooilleen. Haink eh gys y cheirdlann as dooyrt eh: ‘Jean cliwe dou. Ta mee laccal cooilleen.’ Ren y gaaue yn cliwe, agh dooyrt eh: ‘Cha nel treanid ayns cooilleen. Ta treanid ayns jannoo yn red cair.’ Hooar y fer aeg yn roosteyr ayns y clieau. V'eh lane dy treanid: ghow eh yn roosteyr lesh y chliwe ayns e laue, agh cha varr eh eh. Ghow eh yn roosteyr gys y quaiyl, as va'n roosteyr ayns pryssoon son y chooid elley jeh e vea.”

“As va'n gaaue loghtal myr oo hene?” dooyrt Gwenno.

Cha dooyrt Alun veg.

Er laa elley, dooyrt Gwenno: “Cre'n yiarn s'creoi 'sy theihll?”

“Cha nel eh ny yiarn,” dooyrt Alun. “Ta tungsten ny s'creoi na yiarn. Ta tungsten ayns greieyn son giarrey clagh. Agh ta tungsten ro chreoi son aile ny keirdlann shoh.”

Lurg mee, ren Gwenno crou er e lomarcan. Ghow Alun yn crou ayns e laue as yeeagh eh er. “Mie dy liooar,” dooyrt eh. Va'n eddin echey loghtal, agh va boggey ayns e hooillyn.

Feyshtyn:
C'raad ta keirdlann Alun Rattray?
Ta'n cheirdlann echey ayns Ballaugh, faggys da'n cheeill.
Cre ta crou cabbil jeant jeh?
Ta crou cabbil jeant jeh yiarn.
Cre va'n fer aeg 'sy skeeal laccal?
V'eh laccal cooilleen son baase e ayr.
Cre'n treanid va ec y fer aeg?
Ghow eh yn roosteyr gys y quaiyl, agh cha varr eh eh.
Cre'n fa nagh vel Alun gobbraghey lesh tungsten?
Ta tungsten ro chreoi son aile y cheirdlann.

lessons.title: Sheeabin as cainleyn ayns Pheeil
lessons.summary: Briallen Hosking makes soap and candles in a small workshop behind her house in Peel, and her nephew Barra helps her for a week in the summer; she explains that her grandmother made soap from greasy fat that smelt foul when it was melting, while she now uses oil and puts ginger in it for a good smell; she warns Barra that the oil is flammable, and tells him that old matches had phosphorus in them, which was flammable and poisonous; they fill glass bottles with liquid soap, a woman at the market pays with banknotes, and Briallen now exports her soap to England and America.
lessons.text:
Ta Briallen Hosking jannoo sheeabin as cainleyn. Ta keirdlann veg eck cooyl e thie ayns Pheeil. 'Sy tourey shoh, haink y mac-shayrey eck, Barra, dy obbraghey 'sy cheirdlann son shiaghtin. T'eh kiare bleeaney jeig d'eash.

“She keird shenn eh jannoo sheeabin,” dooyrt Briallen. “Ren my shenn-voir sheeabin 'sy chuishlin eck. V'ee goaill feill sahllagh as v'ee lheie eh er yn aile. Va'n feill sahllagh breinn tra v'ee lheie. Va'n soar breinn ayns yn thie ooilley!”

“Vel oo jannoo sheeabin lesh feill sahllagh?” dooyrt Barra.

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Briallen. “Ta mee jannoo sheeabin lesh ooil. Cha nel yn ooil breinn. As ta mee cur jinshar 'sy sheeabin. Ta soar mie ec jinshar.” Hug ee meer jinshar ayns laue Barra. Va'n soar çheh as millish.

Hie ad gys y voayrd. Va saase mooar lane dy ooil er yn aile. “Gow kiarail,” dooyrt Briallen. “Ta'n ooil lossanagh. My ta'n ooil ro çheh, foddee eh goll ayns aile. Ta'n kere son ny cainleyn lossanagh myrgeddin.” Va brat mooar faggys da'n aile, son y fa shen.

Ghow Barra maidjey beg dy aile y hoilshaghey fo'n saase. “Dy henney, va fosfaar er kione dagh maidjey,” dooyrt Briallen. “Va'n fosfaar feer lossanagh, as v'eh nieunagh myrgeddin. Va ny mraane va jannoo maidjey aile ayns Lunnin ching kyndagh rish y fosfaar. Nish, cha nel y fosfaar shen ayn.”

Er y nah laa, ren ad sheeabin fliugh. Ren Barra boteilyn gless y lhieeney. Va jinshar ayns yn sheeabin fliugh myrgeddin. Hug eh lipaid er dagh voteil. Lurg y laa, va daeed boteil er y voayrd.

Er y Jesarn, hie ad gys y margey ayns Pheeil lesh ny boteilyn as y sheeabin creoi. Haink ben gys y voayrd. Ghow ee boteil as daa veer sheeabin jinshar. Hug ee daa noatey da Briallen. Ghow Barra ny noataghyn, as hug eh yn argid elley j'ee.

“Vel oo creck yn sheeabin agh ayns Pheeil?” dooyrt Barra.

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Briallen. “Ta mee assphurtal y sheeabin gys Sostyn as gys America. Ta mee creck eh er y Eddyr-voggyl. Dagh shiaghtin, ta mee assphurtal kiare feed boteil.”

“As vel ad cur noataghyn dhyt ayns America?” dooyrt Barra.

Ren Briallen gearey. “Cha nel. Ta'n argid çheet trooid y Eddyr-voggyl.”

Feyshtyn:
C'raad ta keirdlann Briallen?
Ta keirdlann veg eck cooyl e thie ayns Pheeil.
Cre'n fa va'n thie breinn tra va'n shenn-voir jannoo sheeabin?
V'ee lheie feill sahllagh, as va'n feill sahllagh breinn.
Cre ta Briallen cur 'sy sheeabin son soar mie?
T'ee cur jinshar 'sy sheeabin.
Cre'n fa ta brat mooar faggys da'n aile?
Ta'n ooil as y kere lossanagh.
Cre va er kione dagh maidjey dy henney?
Va fosfaar er, as v'eh lossanagh as nieunagh.
Cre hug y ven da Briallen 'sy vargey?
Hug ee daa noatey j'ee.
C'raad ta Briallen assphurtal y sheeabin?
T'ee assphurtal eh gys Sostyn as gys America.

lessons.title: Yn gansee son Siwan
lessons.summary: Grainne Dowling, eighty-four, still knits fishermen's jumpers in her old age in Laxey, and her granddaughter Siwan comes to learn; Grainne explains that each fishing family had its own pattern and shows her a rare pattern from her mother; she joins the sleeves to the body; they go to the friendly knitting group in the village hall, where Siwan is a guest; Grainne tells how her grandmother worked in a hosiery workshop and wore a tight corset, and how her great-grandmother knitted a jumper for Queen Victoria's jubilee year; at home Grainne makes sweet rice with milk, and the jumper for Siwan is finished in the spring.
lessons.text:
Ta Grainne Dowling kiare bleeaney as kiare feed d'eash. T'ee cummal ayns Laksaa. Ayns e shenneraght, t'ee foast fee ganseeyn. Dy henney, ren ee gansee son dagh eeasteyr 'sy lught-thie eck.

'Sy gheurey shoh, haink Siwan, inneen e mac, dys y thie eck. “Ta mee laccal gynsaghey dy fee gansee,” dooyrt Siwan.

“Mie dy liooar,” dooyrt Grainne. “T'ou aeg, as ta mee ayns my shenneraght. She traa eh.”

Ghow Grainne lioar veg ass e chishtey. Va clowanyn ayn, screeuit lesh laue. “Dy henney, va clowan e hene ec dagh lught-thie dy eeasteyryn,” dooyrt ee. “Va gansee er lheh ec dagh eeasteyr. Shoh clowan anvennick. Va'n clowan shoh ec my voir. Cha nel eh ec sleih elley. T'eh feer anvennick nish.”

Ghow ad ollan gorrym. Hie Grainne er fee dy tappee. Va Siwan fee dy moal. Ta'n gansee jeant ayns daa ayrn. Lurg shiaghtin, va'n chied ayrn jeant, as lurg shiaghtin elley, yn nah ayrn. “Nish ta shin sniemmey ny daa ayrn ry-cheilley,” dooyrt Grainne. Ren ad sniemmey yn gansee ry-cheilley lesh snaie gorrym.

Er y Jeheiney, hie ad gys thie y valley. Ta possan dy vraane fee ayns shen dagh shiaghtin. Va Siwan ny cuirreydagh. Va ny mraane caarjoil. “Failt ort. Ta shin possan caarjoil,” dooyrt ad rish y chuirreydagh. Hug ad tey as arran j'ee. Va ad feer caarjoil.

Dooyrt Grainne rish ny mraane: “Va my shenn-voir gobbraghey ayns keirdlann oashyraght ayns Doolish. V'ee jannoo oashyraght, eaddagh son ny cassyn. Va ram mraane ayns y cheirdlann oashyraght. As va sheeinteyder urree dagh laa. Va'n sheeinteyder feer çhionn. Cha row ee abyl dy ee monney!”

Ren ny mraane gearey. “Ta sheeinteyder ec my voir ayns y thie foast,” dooyrt ben elley. “T'eh anvennick nish.”

“As va my shenn-shenn-voir fee gansee son Blein Feayslee yn Venrein Victoria,” dooyrt Grainne. “She 1887 v'ayn. Va gansee jiarg ec dagh eeasteyr ayns Laksaa son y Vlein Feayslee.”

Tra haink ad thie, ren Grainne reise millish lesh bainney. “She shoh bee my shenneraght,” dooyrt ee. “Reise millish as tey.”

'Sy arragh, va'n gansee jeant. Hug Siwan e gansee gorrym urree. Va'n clowan anvennick er. “Nish t'ou ny eeasteyr firrinagh,” dooyrt Grainne.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Grainne jannoo ayns e shenneraght?
T'ee foast fee ganseeyn.
Cre'n clowan va ec moir Grainne?
Va clowan anvennick eck, nagh vel ec sleih elley.
Cre ren Grainne as Siwan lesh ny daa ayrn?
Ren ad sniemmey ny daa ayrn ry-cheilley.
Cre'n fa va Siwan ny cuirreydagh?
Hie ee gys possan ny mraane son y chied cheayrt.
C'raad va shenn-voir Grainne gobbraghey?
V'ee gobbraghey ayns keirdlann oashyraght ayns Doolish.
Cre ren Grainne tra haink ad thie?
Ren ee reise millish lesh bainney.

lessons.title: Meillaghyn fuygh
lessons.summary: Hedd Penhaligon turns wooden bowls in Sulby from the pear trees and cherry trees of old gardens; the collector Dougal Ferrier comes to buy a bowl, and they talk about the look of a bowl and about creativity; Dougal shows Hedd an old bowl of palm wood that he bought in Chad, and a knife with an ivory handle that was his grandfather's; he explains that selling new ivory is banned now to save the elephants; Hedd says a bowl is not only aesthetic but made to be used, and Dougal buys a cherry bowl and a pear bowl.
lessons.text:
Ta Hedd Penhaligon jannoo meillaghyn fuygh ayns Sulby. Ta'n fuygh echey çheet veih garaghyn shenn. Tra ta billey peear ny billey shillish goll er giarrey sheese, ta sleih cur y fuygh da Hedd.

“Ta fuygh peear bane as mean,” dooyrt Hedd. “Ta fuygh y shillish jiarg as dhone, as t'eh dorraghey lurg tammylt. She fuygh mie t'ayn son meilley.”

Er y Jeheiney, haink fer noa gys y cheirdlann. She Dougal Ferrier va'n ennym echey. V'eh ny çhagleyder. “Ta mee çhaglym meillaghyn,” dooyrt eh. “Ta meillaghyn aym veih dagh çheer 'sy theihll. Ta mee laccal meilley veih Ellan Vannin.”

Yeeagh Dougal er ny meillaghyn er y voayrd. Ghow eh meilley shillish ayns e laue. “T'eh aalin,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n cummey aesthetagh. Ta mee çhaglym meillaghyn er son y cummey aesthetagh oc.”

“Ta'n cummey scanshoil,” dooyrt Hedd. “Agh cha nel meilley agh aesthetagh. Ta meilley jeant dy ve ymmydit, son bainney, son mess, son arran. Ta crootaght ayns jannoo red mie as red ymmydagh ry-cheilley.”

“Shen crootaght firrinagh,” dooyrt y çhagleyder.

Ghow Dougal meilley beg dhone ass e phoagey. “Shoh meilley jeant jeh palm,” dooyrt eh. “Chionnee mee eh ayns Shad, ayns margey beg. Ta biljyn palm ayns jiass Shad. Ta fuygh y phalm creoi as feddanagh, as t'eh doillee dy obbraghey.” Ghow Hedd y meilley palm. V'eh eddrym, as va daah aalin er.

Eisht ghow Dougal skynn shenn. Va laue iuaagagh er. Va'n laue iuaagagh bane as myn. “Va'n skynn shoh ec my shenn-ayr,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n laue iuaagagh jeant jeh feeacklyn elefant. Nish, ta creck iuaagagh noa meelowit ayns ymmodee çheeraghyn. Ta'n leigh dy meelowal yn chreck shen sauail ny elefantyn.”

“Vel oo foast çhaglym reddyn iuaagagh?” dooyrt Hedd.

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Dougal. “Ta mee çhaglym meillaghyn fuygh nish. Cha nel fuygh meelowit.” Ren ad gearey.

Lurg shen, chionnee Dougal daa veilley: meilley shillish jiarg as meilley peear bane. Hug eh noataghyn da Hedd. “Bee ad 'sy chishtey-gless aym,” dooyrt y çhagleyder, “eddyr y meilley palm veih Shad as meilley veih'n Clyst Iuaagagh.”

Feyshtyn:
C'raad ta fuygh Hedd çheet veih?
T'eh çheet veih garaghyn shenn, veih biljyn peear as biljyn shillish.
Cre'n daah t'er fuygh y shillish?
Ta fuygh y shillish jiarg as dhone.
Cre'n fa ta Dougal çhaglym meillaghyn?
T'eh çhaglym ad er son y cummey aesthetagh oc.
Cre ta Hedd gra mychione crootaght?
Ta crootaght ayns jannoo red mie as red ymmydagh ry-cheilley.
C'raad chionnee Dougal y meilley palm?
Chionnee eh eh ayns margey beg ayns Shad.
Cre'n fa ta creck iuaagagh noa meelowit?
Ta'n leigh sauail ny elefantyn.

lessons.title: Y baie corranagh er y charmeish
lessons.summary: Fergal Cormack paints scenery for a film that is being made in Peel; he must paint a crescent-shaped bay on a huge canvas for the set, so he draws a grid on his small picture and on the canvas and copies one square at a time, with small figures of fishermen on the shore; he learned the craft from his grandfather Ewart, an engraver who made geographical maps, and who painted camouflage on ships in the war, saying a ship must be like a chameleon; when the canvas stands on the set, the director cannot tell it from the real bay.
lessons.text:
Ta Fergal Cormack ny pheinteyr. T'eh peintal reddyn son scannaneyn. 'Sy vlein shoh, ta scannane goll er jannoo ayns Pheeil, as ta Fergal gobbraghey er y sett.

Er y chied laa, dooyrt y stiureyder rish: “Ta baie corranagh shirrit orrin son y sett. Ta'n baie ayns y scannane gollrish yn eayst noa: t'eh corranagh. Peint y baie corranagh er carmeish vooar.”

Va'n charmeish feer vooar, ny smoo na boalley thie. Hug ad y charmeish ny shassoo cooyl y sett. Va jalloo beg ec Fergal, jalloo jeh'n vaie. Agh kys oddagh eh y jalloo beg y chur er y charmeish vooar?

Ren Fergal ingagh er y jalloo beg. Ren eh linnaghyn jeeragh seose as sheese, as linnaghyn elley harrish. Eisht ren eh ingagh mooar er y charmeish, lesh yn earroo cheddin dy rheynnyn. “Nish ta mee peintal un rheynn dy cheayrt,” dooyrt eh. “Lesh yn ingagh, cha nel yn obbyr doillee.”

Va figgyryn beggey 'sy jalloo: eeasteyryn er y traie, as ben as paitçhey. Ren Fergal ny figgyryn er y charmeish, figgyr lurg figgyr.

Ghow Fergal yn cheird veih e henn-ayr, Ewart Cormack. Va Ewart ny linneyder. Ren y linneyder kaartyn çheeroaylleeagh: kaartyn jeh'n ellan, jeh ny sleityn as jeh ny awinyn. “Ta kaart çheeroaylleeagh feer kiart,” dooyrt Ewart rish dy mennick. “Ta'n linneyder jannoo dagh linney dy kiart.” As ren y linneyder ingagh er dagh kaart çheeroaylleeagh myrgeddin.

'Sy chaggey, ren Ewart obbyr elley: keiltynys. Ren eh peintal lhongyn son keiltynys. Ren eh linnaghyn mooarey glass, gorrym as bane er ny lhongyn. “Ta lhong lesh keiltynys mie gollrish kameelyan,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n kameelyan caghlaa e ghaah, as cha nel y noid fakin eh. Shen myr ta keiltynys.”

Ren Fergal smooinaghtyn er y kameelyan tra v'eh peintal y keayn er y charmeish. Va'n keayn glass as gorrym, myr lhongyn e henn-ayr.

Lurg three shiaghteeyn, va'n charmeish jeant. Haink y stiureyder dys y sett. Yeeagh eh er y baie corranagh er y charmeish, as er ny figgyryn er y traie. “Cha nod mee fakin cre'n baie ta firrinagh, as cre'n baie ta er y charmeish,” dooyrt eh. Va boggey er Fergal.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta shirrit son y sett?
Ta baie corranagh shirrit, peintit er carmeish vooar.
Cre ren Fergal er y jalloo beg as er y charmeish?
Ren eh ingagh er y jalloo beg as ingagh mooar er y charmeish.
Cre ny figgyryn va 'sy jalloo?
Va eeasteyryn er y traie, as ben as paitçhey.
Cre ren Ewart Cormack myr linneyder?
Ren eh kaartyn çheeroaylleeagh jeh'n ellan.
Cre'n fa ren Ewart peintal ny lhongyn 'sy chaggey?
Ren eh peintal ad son keiltynys, nagh vod y noid fakin ad.
Cre dooyrt y stiureyder mychione y charmeish?
Cha dod eh fakin cre'n baie va firrinagh.

lessons.title: Yn baatey ymmyrtagh noa
lessons.summary: Lleucu Baird becomes the new leader of the rowing club in Ramsey and reorganises it: training twice a week, a target of a race in Douglas Bay in August, and more activity for the young members; the club asks the boatbuilder Hywel Pendry for a new wooden rowing boat, and he builds it on a strong base of oak from an inland wood and explains momentum to the rowers; the club is busy all summer, they carry the new boat down a steep path to the shore for the first time, and at the race they come second and are happy.
lessons.text:
Ta club ymmyrt ayns Rhumsaa. Dy henney, va'n club tarroogh, agh ayns ny bleeantyn s'jerree, cha row monney bioyrid ayn. Va'n baatey ymmyrtagh shenn, as cha row ny sleih aegey çheet.

'Sy vlein shoh, ghow Lleucu Baird yn club ayns laue. Ren ee aareaghey yn club ooilley. “Ta shin aareaghey yn club ayns three aghtyn,” dooyrt ee rish ny olteynyn. “Ta aareaghey feer ymmyrçhagh. Hed shin ymmyrt daa cheayrt 'sy hiaghtin. Bee bioyrid noa ayn son ny sleih aegey. As bee targad ain: yn ratçh ayns Baie Ghoolish ayns Luanistyn.”

“Shen targad mooar,” dooyrt fer jeh ny olteynyn. “Cha nel baatey mie ain.”

“Bee baatey noa ain,” dooyrt Lleucu.

Hie ee gys Hywel Pendry. Ta Hywel jannoo lhongyn beggey fuygh, myr ren e ayr roish. “Ta baatey ymmyrtagh noa shirrit orrin,” dooyrt Lleucu. “Vel oo abyl dy yannoo eh roish Luanistyn?”

“Ta,” dooyrt Hywel. “Agh bee mee tarroogh.”

Ren Hywel toshiaght lesh yn undin. “Ta'n undin yn ayrn s'scanshoil jeh'n vaatey,” dooyrt eh. “My ta'n undin lajer, bee'n baatey lajer.” Va'n undin jeant jeh darragh. Haink y darragh veih keyll antraieagh, foddey veih'n cheayn. “Ta'n darragh veih keyll antraieagh creoi,” dooyrt Hywel.

Haink ny sleih aegey dys y cheirdlann dy akin y baatey. Dooyrt Hywel roo: “Tra ta shiu ymmyrt, ta'n baatey goll roish. Eddyr dagh tayrn, ta'n baatey foast gleashagh. She shen momentum. My ta shiu ymmyrt ry-cheilley, ta'n momentum mooar. My ta shiu ymmyrt dy olk, ta'n momentum goll ersooyl.”

Va'n club tarroogh son y tourey ooilley. Va bioyrid ayn dagh fastyr. Va ny sleih aegey ymmyrt 'sy vaatey shenn, as ymmyrt ry-cheilley, son y momentum.

Ayns Jerrey Souree, va'n baatey noa jeant. Va raad eaynagh veih'n cheirdlann sheese gys y traie. Ghow kiare deiney as kiare mraane y baatey ayns nyn laueyn. Hie ad sheese y raad eaynagh dy moal. “Gow kiarail!” dooyrt Hywel. “Ta'n raad eaynagh fliugh.” Hug ad y baatey 'sy cheayn son y chied cheayrt. Hie eh dy mie.

Ayns Luanistyn, va'n ratçh ayns Baie Ghoolish. Ren yn club ymmyrt dy lajer. Cha row ad ny chied: v'ad ny nah. Agh va boggey er Lleucu. “Va'n targad ain dy ve 'sy ratçh,” dooyrt ee. “As ta shin ayn.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa nagh row monney bioyrid 'sy club?
Va'n baatey shenn, as cha row ny sleih aegey çheet.
Cre'n targad hug Lleucu er y club?
Hug ee targad er y club: yn ratçh ayns Baie Ghoolish ayns Luanistyn.
Cre'n fa ta'n undin scanshoil?
My ta'n undin lajer, bee'n baatey lajer.
C'raad haink y darragh veih?
Haink eh veih keyll antraieagh, foddey veih'n cheayn.
Cre ta momentum, rere Hywel?
Eddyr dagh tayrn, ta'n baatey foast gleashagh: shen momentum.
Kys hie y baatey noa gys y traie?
Ghow ad eh ayns nyn laueyn sheese y raad eaynagh.

lessons.title: Mill as freoagh
lessons.summary: Jenkin Rescorla keeps bees on a farm near Andreas and makes their hives by hand in the old way; his bees take nectar from the yellow charlock in the fields in spring and from the heather on the hills in late summer; his neighbour Rennie Dunlop keeps poultry and sells chickens to the butcher in Ramsey; one day a bee stings Rennie and he cannot breathe well, so Jenkin drives him to the hospital, where the doctor gives him medicine and says that Jenkin has a kind of immunity after many years; Rennie's wife calls it a miracle, the doctor says it was quick help; and Jenkin explains that the squirrel on his honey label is for his grandmother, because there are no squirrels on the island.
lessons.text:
Ta Jenkin Rescorla freayll shellanyn er thalloo faggys da Andreas. Ta keird shenn echey myrgeddin: t'eh jannoo thieyn son ny shellanyn lesh e laueyn hene, myr ren sleih dy henney.

'Syn arragh, ta brashlagh buigh fassaghey ayns ny magheryn. “Ta ny shellanyn goaill naghtyr veih'n brashlagh,” dooyrt Jenkin. “Ta'n naghtyr 'sy vlaa. Ta'n shellan goaill y naghtyr dys y thie, as ta'n naghtyr goll er jannoo mill.” Ta'n mill veih'n brashlagh bane as creoi. Ta brashlagh ry-akin er dagh magher.

Ayns jerrey'n tourey, ta Jenkin goaill ny shellanyn seose gys ny sleityn. Ta'n freoagh ayns blaa ayns shen. Ta'n mill veih'n freoagh dorraghey as feer villish. “She mill y freoagh yn mill share,” dooyrt Jenkin.

Ta naboo echey, Rennie Dunlop. Ta Rennie freayll eeanlee: kiarkyn as thunnagyn. T'eh creck ny eeanlee da'n buitçhoor ayns Rhumsaa. Ta'n buitçhoor creck feill as eeanlee 'sy thie-creck echey.

Un laa, haink Rennie dy chionnaghey mill. Hug shellan guinn er laue Rennie. Lurg minnid, cha row Rennie abyl dy goaill ennal dy mie. Va'n laue echey mooar as jiarg.

“Ta shin goll gys y lheelann,” dooyrt Jenkin. Ghow eh Rennie 'sy charr dys y lheelann ayns Rhumsaa. Ec y lheelann, hug y fer-lheihys lheihys da Rennie. Lurg oor, v'eh abyl dy goaill ennal reesht.

“Va shiu tappee,” dooyrt y fer-lheihys. “Vel guinn ny shellanyn doillee dhyt hene?”

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Jenkin. “Ta mee freayll shellanyn son daeed blein. Cha nel guinn ny shellanyn jannoo monney orrym nish.”

“Ta jeenaght ayd,” dooyrt y fer-lheihys. “Lurg ram bleeantyn, ta jeenaght ec paart dy leih. Agh cha nel jeenaght ec Rennie. Cha lhisagh eh goll faggys da ny shellanyn.”

Haink ben Rennie dys y lheelann. “She mirril eh!” dooyrt ee. “Mirril veih Jee!”

“Cha nel mirril erbee ayn,” dooyrt y fer-lheihys. “Haink eh dys y lheelann dy tappee, as va lheihys ain. Shen ooilley.”

Lurg shiaghtin, va Rennie mie reesht. Hug eh daa chiark da Jenkin, as hug Jenkin mill y freoagh da.

Yeeagh Rennie er y lipaid er y mill. Va jalloo fiorag jiarg er. “Cre'n fa ta fiorag er y lipaid?” dooyrt eh. “Cha nel fiorag erbee ayns Ellan Vannin.”

“Va my shenn-voir veih Nalbin,” dooyrt Jenkin. “Va fioragyn 'sy cheyll ec e thie. Va graih eck er ny fioragyn. Shen y fa ta'n fiorag er y mill.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre veih ta ny shellanyn goaill naghtyr 'syn arragh?
T'ad goaill naghtyr veih'n brashlagh buigh ayns ny magheryn.
Cre'n mill share, rere Jenkin?
She mill y freoagh yn mill share.
Cre ta Rennie Dunlop jannoo lesh ny eeanlee?
T'eh creck ad da'n buitçhoor ayns Rhumsaa.
Cre'n fa hie Rennie gys y lheelann?
Hug shellan guinn er e laue, as cha row eh abyl dy goaill ennal dy mie.
Cre'n fa nagh vel guinn ny shellanyn jannoo monney er Jenkin?
Ta jeenaght echey lurg daeed blein lesh shellanyn.
Cre'n fa ta fiorag er y lipaid?
Va graih ec shenn-voir Jenkin er ny fioragyn ayns Nalbin.

lessons.title: Yn fiddyl noa
lessons.summary: Rhydian Carne makes fiddles in a small workshop in Onchan and has a certificate from a school of instrument making; Kenna Skene, who leads a young string quartet, asks him for a new fiddle; he explains that a fiddle is made of simple things, and that the acoustic quality comes from the wood and its shape; Kenna explains that leadership in a quartet means listening to the other three, and she also plays in a pop music band; a radio broadcaster interviews Rhydian and asks about glory, and he says there is no glory in the craft, only joy; on the evening of the concert Rhydian hears the quartet on the radio with the new fiddle.
lessons.text:
Ta Rhydian Carne jannoo greieyn-kiaull ayns keirdlann veg ayns Onchan. T'eh jannoo fiddyl ny ghaa dagh blein. Ta teishtys er y voalley 'sy cheirdlann echey. Hooar eh yn teishtys veih scoill son jannoo greieyn-kiaull, lurg three bleeaney dy ynsaghey.

Un moghrey, haink Kenna Skene dys y cheirdlann. T'ee ny kiaulleyder, as t'ee ec kione kiaraid aeg: kiare kiaulleyderyn, kiare greieyn-kiaull. “Ta'n kiaraid ain cloie ayns Doolish ayns three meeghyn,” dooyrt ee. “Ta greie noa shirrit orrym.”

“Bee mee tarroogh,” dooyrt Rhydian, “agh nee'm eh.”

Hug eh fuygh er y voayrd. “Ta fiddyl jeant jeh reddyn oney,” dooyrt eh. “Fuygh as teadyn. Ta'n obbyr oney, agh cha nel ee aashagh. Ta'n chooid sheeanoil çheet veih'n fuygh as veih'n cummey. My ta'n fuygh ro hiu, cha nel y sheean mie. My ta'n fuygh ro hanney, ta'n sheean ro lajer. Ta ram bleeantyn shirrit dy ynsaghey yn chooid sheeanoil.”

“Ta kiaull y chiaraid sheeanoil myrgeddin,” dooyrt Kenna. “Ta mee ec kione y chiaraid, agh cha nel leeideiltys jannoo y chooid smoo dy loayrt. Ta leeideiltys ayns eaishtagh rish ny three elley.”

“As vel oo cloie kiaull elley?” dooyrt Rhydian.

Ren Kenna gearey. “Ta. Ta mee cloie ayns possan snagchiaull, ayns thie-oast er y Jesarn. She snagchiaull t'ayn, agh ta'n kiaraid as y snagchiaull mie ry-cheilley.”

Lurg mee, haink creeleyder veih'n radio dys y cheirdlann. Va'n creeleyder laccal loayrt rish Rhydian son y radio. “Ta gloyr ec ny kiaulleyderyn,” dooyrt y creeleyder. “Vel gloyr ayns jannoo greieyn-kiaull?”

“Cha nel gloyr ayn,” dooyrt Rhydian. “Ta'n gloyr ec Kenna, as shen cair. Cha nel ayns my cheird agh boggey.”

Lurg three meeghyn, va'n greie noa jeant. Va'n chooid sheeanoil mie. Va'n kiaraid cloie ayns Doolish, as va'n cloie er y radio. Va Rhydian 'sy thie, as cheayll eh y kiaraid er y radio. Cheayll eh e ghreie noa hene, as cheayll eh Kenna cloie y chied arrane. Lurg y chloie, dooyrt y creeleyder er y radio: “Va fiddyl noa ec Kenna Skene, jeant ayns Onchan.”

Feyshtyn:
C'raad hooar Rhydian yn teishtys echey?
Hooar eh yn teishtys veih scoill son jannoo greieyn-kiaull.
Cre'n fa haink Kenna dys y cheirdlann?
Va greie noa shirrit urree son y kiaraid.
Cre jeh ta fiddyl jeant?
Ta fiddyl jeant jeh reddyn oney: fuygh as teadyn.
C'raad ta'n chooid sheeanoil çheet veih?
T'ee çheet veih'n fuygh as veih'n cummey.
Cre ta leeideiltys, rere Kenna?
Ta leeideiltys ayns eaishtagh rish ny three elley.
Cre dooyrt Rhydian mychione gloyr?
Cha nel gloyr ayns y cheird echey, agh boggey.
Cre cheayll Rhydian er y radio?
Cheayll eh y kiaraid as e ghreie noa hene.

lessons.title: Yn thie-clou shenn
lessons.summary: Seumas Petrie still prints with old wooden letters in a printing house in Castletown, and he tells his daughter Annis how it began: in the 1830s the founder, Quintin Petrie, was a young servant on a big farm, where the farmer mistreated him, scolded him every day and forced him to work sixteen hours; Quintin saw the injustice and ran away to Douglas, where a printer took him as an apprentice; the printer printed a paper for the Whigs, and an intellectual, an exile from Poland, wrote in it about injustice; later, in 1912, Quintin's grandson printed posters for the unionists from Ulster and for their opponents too; Seumas shows Annis the first page that Quintin printed.
lessons.text:
Ta Seumas Petrie ny fer-clou. Ta thie-clou echey ayns Balley Chashtal. T'eh foast prental lesh lettyryn shenn jeh fuygh as jeh leoaie. Er y Jesarn shoh, va'n inneen echey, Annis, 'sy thie-clou marish.

“Quoi ren y thie-clou shoh y chur er bun?” dooyrt Annis.

“Quintin Petrie,” dooyrt Seumas. “She shenn-shenn-ayr my ayr v'ayn. Ayns ny 1830yn, va Quintin ny sharvaant aeg er thalloo mooar. Va'n eirinagh drogh ghooinney. Ren eh caartrey er y sharvaant aeg dagh laa. Ren eh troiddey eh dagh moghrey as dagh fastyr. Va Quintin eignit dy obbraghey shey ooryn jeig 'sy laa. Cha row bee dy liooar echey, ny lhiabbee çheh.”

“Shen aggair,” dooyrt Annis.

“Ta,” dooyrt Seumas. “As honnick Quintin yn aggair. Cha row eh laccal ve ny sharvaant son e vea ooilley. Lurg three bleeaney dy chaartrey as dy troiddey, roie eh ersooyl gys Doolish. Ghow fer-clou ayns Doolish eh. Cha row y fer-clou shen loghtal. Cha ren eh troiddey ny caartrey er Quintin. Ren eh gynsaghey yn cheird da.”

Ghow Seumas pabyr shenn ass kishtey. “Ren y fer-clou shen prental pabyr son y phartee feoiltagh,” dooyrt eh. “Va'n pabyr feoiltagh. Va'n phartee feoiltagh laccal caghlaa 'sy reiltys. Va toiggaltagh screeu 'sy phabyr feoiltagh dagh shiaghtin. V'eh ny eebyrtagh veih Polynn. V'eh eignit dy aagail e çheer. Va'n toiggaltagh screeu mychione aggair: aggair noi sharvaantyn, as aggair noi eebyrtee. Va Quintin cur ny lettyryn echey ry-cheilley son y phabyr.”

“As lurg shen?” dooyrt Annis.

“Ayns 1912, va oe Quintin ec kione y thie-clou. Haink unnaneyseyryn veih Ulster gys Ellan Vannin. Va pabyryn mooarey son y voalley shirrit orroo. Ren yn thie-clou prental ad. Agh ren eh prental pabyryn son y sleih noi ny unnaneyseyryn myrgeddin.”

“Son ny unnaneyseyryn as son nyn noidyn?” dooyrt Annis.

“She fer-clou ta prental son dagh unnane,” dooyrt Seumas. Ren eh gearey. Eisht ghow eh pabyr beg veih'n voalley. “Shoh yn chied phabyr ren Quintin prental, ayns 1839. T'eh screeuit er: ‘Cha nel sharvaant erbee eignit.’”

Feyshtyn:
C'raad ta thie-clou Seumas Petrie?
T'eh ayns Balley Chashtal.
Cre va Quintin ayns ny 1830yn?
V'eh ny sharvaant aeg er thalloo mooar.
Cre ren yn eirinagh rish Quintin?
Ren eh caartrey er, ren eh troiddey eh, as va Quintin eignit dy obbraghey shey ooryn jeig 'sy laa.
Quoi va screeu 'sy phabyr feoiltagh?
Va toiggaltagh screeu ayn, eebyrtagh veih Polynn.
Quoi haink veih Ulster ayns 1912?
Haink unnaneyseyryn veih Ulster.
Cre va screeuit er y chied phabyr?
Va screeuit er: ‘Cha nel sharvaant erbee eignit.’

lessons.title: Sooillagyn son ny rollageyn
lessons.summary: Alasdair Moyle, a retired teacher near Cregneash, grinds lenses by hand for telescopes and microscopes, an old craft he learned from a book in German, with an umlaut on the word on the cover; his grandson Lachie stays with him in winter; first they look through a microscope at water from a pond and see an amoeba change its shape; Alasdair has an experimental lens of a new shape and a theory that it will give a clearer picture; at night they put it in the aluminium tube of the telescope, find a minor planet moving among the stars, and Alasdair explains the eccentricity of its orbit and the cosmic rays from far away; the experimental lens is good, and Lachie writes everything in a notebook.
lessons.text:
Va Alasdair Moyle ny ynseyder roish. Nish t'eh cummal ayns thie beg faggys da Cregneash. Ta keird anvennick echey: t'eh jannoo sooillagyn lesh e laueyn, son fodreayrtanyn as son mynreayrtanyn. Ren eh gynsaghey yn cheird veih lioar shenn ayns Germaanish. Va umlaut 'sy chied fockle er y lioar: daa phoynt beggey harrish lettyr.

“Cre ta umlaut?” dooyrt Lachie, oe Alasdair. Va Lachie çheet dy hannaghtyn rish son shiaghtin 'sy gheurey.

“Ta umlaut caghlaa sheean y lettyr,” dooyrt Alasdair. “Ta umlautyn ayns ram fockleyn Germaanish. Cha nel umlaut erbee 'sy Ghaelg.”

Er y chied laa, ghow ad ushtey veih loghan beg faggys da'n thie. Hug Alasdair bine dy ushtey fo'n mynreayrtan. “Jeeagh,” dooyrt eh. Yeeagh Lachie. Va red beg 'syn ushtey, red bio. V'eh caghlaa e chummey dy moal. “She amoeba t'ayn,” dooyrt Alasdair. “Cha nel agh un chillag ayns amoeba. T'eh gleashagh liorish caghlaa e chummey.”

“T'eh feer anaasagh,” dooyrt Lachie. Yeeagh eh er yn amoeba son lieh oor.

Er y nah laa, ghow Alasdair sooillag noa ass kishtey. “She sooillag treealagh t'ayn,” dooyrt eh. “Ta cummey noa urree. Ta sursmooinaght aym: ta mee credjal dy der y cummey noa jalloo ny smoo glen. Agh she sursmooinaght ny lomarcan eh. Cha nel fys aym foast.”

'Syn oie, va'n speyr glen as dorraghey. Hug ad y sooillag treealagh 'sy fodreayrtan. Va feddan y fodreayrtan jeant jeh ollymin. “Ta ollymin eddrym as lajer,” dooyrt Alasdair. Yeeagh ad er ny rollageyn. Va ram rollageyn ayn. Eisht hooar Alasdair red beg, gollrish rollage, agh v'eh gleashagh dy moal mastey ny rollageyn.

“She mynphlanaid t'ayn,” dooyrt eh. “Ta ram mynphlanaidyn goll mygeayrt y Ghrian. Ta'n raad echey mygeayrt y Ghrian gollrish ooh, as cha nel eh cruinn. She corrid ta shin gra rish shen. Ta corrid vooar ec y mynphlanaid shoh. T'eh anaasagh dy liooar.”

“As cre ta goll trooid y speyr eddyr ny rollageyn?” dooyrt Lachie.

“Ta scellyn tuinnagh çheet veih foddey ersooyl, trooid y speyr,” dooyrt Alasdair. “Cha nod shin fakin ny scellyn tuinnagh shoh. Agh t'ad goll trooid y thalloo as trooid ain hene dagh laa.”

Va'n jalloo trooid y sooillag treealagh feer ghlen. “Va'n sursmooinaght ayd kiart!” dooyrt Lachie. Screeu eh dy chooilley red ayns lioar veg: yn amoeba, yn umlaut, as y mynphlanaid lesh y corrid vooar.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Alasdair Moyle jannoo lesh e laueyn?
T'eh jannoo sooillagyn son fodreayrtanyn as son mynreayrtanyn.
Cre ta umlaut?
Ta umlaut daa phoynt beggey harrish lettyr, as t'eh caghlaa sheean y lettyr.
Cre honnick Lachie fo'n mynreayrtan?
Honnick eh amoeba caghlaa e chummey 'syn ushtey.
Cre'n sursmooinaght t'ec Alasdair?
T'eh credjal dy der y sooillag treealagh jalloo ny smoo glen.
Cre ta goll trooid y speyr veih foddey ersooyl?
Ta scellyn tuinnagh goll trooid y speyr.
Cre jeh ta feddan y fodreayrtan jeant?
T'eh jeant jeh ollymin.
Cre ta corrid?
She corrid t'ayn tra ta'n raad mygeayrt y Ghrian gollrish ooh, as nagh vel eh cruinn.
